title: HTMLImageElement.decode() is not clear about what frame the animated image will tie its completion with resolving the returned promise
body:
This issue is related to #1920.

> Animated images will become completely available only after all their frames are loaded. Thus, even though an implementation could decode the first frame before that point, the above steps will not do so, instead waiting until all frames are available.
> https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#dom-img-decode

This implies that calling decode() will request decoding the first frame of an animated image always. The problem is that since we only want to keep around the frames required to produce the next image frame, rewinding the playback to frame_0 can cause the decoder to flush its cache. This is especially bad if you were on a frame with a high count, such as frame_100, because now you'll have to decode 101 frames to play the next frame.

In this case it's unlikely that the user called decode() to force frame_0. Rather they just wanted to ensure that there was a frame ready to display.

> User agents should ensure that the decoded media data stays readily available until at least the end of the next update the rendering step in the event loop. This is an important part of the API contract, and should not be broken if at all possible.
> https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#dom-img-decode

This implies that the promise of the decode() function has to be resolved immediately after finishing the decoding of the requested frame. In other words it has to fire even before the frame of the animated image is displayed in the page. This will guarantee the availability of the frame at least until at least the end of the next update the rendering step in the event loop. 

I propose the following changes:

- Calling decode() on an animated image will return a Promise that resolves when a new frame of image data has been decoded.

- For an animated image that has never started animation, this will decode frame_0.
- For an animated image that is currently animating, it will be the next frame from the current point of animation.
